title: Fix edge-case causing negative burst allowance in Dedicated autoscaler utilization reporting
author: Priya Patel
description: Context: The Dedicated autoscaler emits per-fleet utilization and burst allowance metrics used by billing and capacity routing. We observed a small class of requests (very short-lived emergencies where node drains and immediate scaledown coincide) that produced a transient negative 'burst_allowance' value in the utilization report. This caused downstream consumers (billing and the fleet-health pipeline) to treat the fleet as having extra debt and temporarily throttle priority lanes. Root cause: when zero-duration windows were processed, floating-point rounding combined with the tokenbucket refill math could produce -epsilon allowance which was serialized as a small negative number instead of clamped to 0.0. Change: 1) Clamp burst allowance and computed available_tokens to be >= 0 after tokenbucket math. 2) Normalize the utilization-reporting pipeline to apply the clamp before aggregation and expose the pre-clamp / post-clamp fields for debugging (hidden behind a flag). 3) Add a regression test that simulates node drain + immediate scale-from-zero to ensure no negative allowances are emitted. 4) Add telemetry counters for "clamp_applied" and a short-term alert to monitor rate of clamping in prod. Notes: The description includes reason and rollout plan. Rollout: feature flag gated (autoscaler.fix_negative_burst_allowance), staged rollout: Canary (10% fleets) -> ramp to 50% -> 100% over 48 hours, with automatic rollback if clamp_applied rate exceeds 0.1% of reports in a 5m window. This PR is strictly a bugfix with a small metric addition; no API contract changes.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) fix: clamp tokenbucket negative allowance and add unit tests; 2) feat(telemetry): add clamp_applied counter and expose debug fields behind flag; 3) test: add integration/regression test simulating drain + immediate scale-from-zero.
diff_snippets: services/autoscaler/src/tokenbucket.rs: clamp available_tokens = available_tokens.max(0.0); // prevent negative allowances
services/autoscaler/src/reporting.rs: if cfg.feature("autoscaler.fix_negative_burst_allowance") { expose debug fields: pre_clamp_allowance }

release_notes: Bugfix: Prevent negative burst allowance values in Dedicated autoscaler utilization reports which could cause transient priority throttling. Adds a short-term telemetry counter 'autoscaler.clamp_applied' and a debug flag for pre/post clamp values.
deployment_notes: Gate behind feature flag autoscaler.clamp_negative_allowance. Start canary on 10% fleets for 2h, monitor clamp_applied and p95 latency of reporting pipeline. Ramp to 50% over 6h then 100% over 48h if no regressions.
qa_steps: Deploy to staging with feature flag on and simulate node drains to ensure no negative burst_allowance emitted
Verify metrics autoscaler.clamp_applied is 0 for normal workloads and increments when clamp would have been applied in synthetic tests
notes: This PR was driven by a customer incident SUP-889 where priority traffic experienced unexpected throttling. No schema changes to reports; added optional debug fields behind flag only.
